widgets_values:
Playground: MATCH TWO VIEWS OVER A MASK.

The blueprint 'CV Exposure Match (Masked Per-Channel)' makes one image
agree with another, per BGR channel, over the region a mask selects:

    corrected = (x - mean_A) * sigma_B / max(sigma_A, 0.5) + mean_B

meanStdDev packs its per-channel results into one length-4 vector, and
cv2 arithmetic broadcasts that AS a per-channel Scalar - so three gains
and three offsets cost one node each. The 0.5 floor on sigma keeps a
flat channel from dividing by ~zero. The MASK is the whole idea: it
says WHERE the two images must agree, and the fit is then applied
everywhere.

THE CASE SHOWN HERE: TILED PROCESSING. Run any statistics-dependent
operator per tile instead of once over the whole image and the tiles
stop agreeing - each one measured its own histogram. Nothing in this
graph darkens or tints anything; the drift is what the operator does.
Row 1 runs xphoto white balance ('simple') on the whole page, then on
each half separately: the halves land on different per-channel gains
(tile 1 ~0.39/0.57/0.58, tile 2 ~1.03/1.01/1.01) and the reassembled
page carries a 56-grey-level step down its middle. Matching each tile
to the WHOLE-IMAGE pass over that tile's own mask removes it: mean
deviation from the single-pass result 14.3 -> 0.8, seam step 56 -> 0.4.
That is the production idiom - a tiled render is colour-matched against
a cheap global (or low-res) pass, tile by tile.

ROW 2 IS THE NEGATIVE, and it uses the identical wiring. CLAHE per tile
drifts too, but a per-tile TONE CURVE is not a gain and an offset, so
the match has nothing to grab: deviation 7.3 -> 7.4 (i.e. nothing) and
the seam does not improve either (13 -> 15). Same node, same masks,
no result - the fit has to match the SHAPE of the drift.

OTHER JOBS FOR THIS NODE, same 'where must they agree' question:
  * clean-plate / change detection - mask = the region that must be
    UNCHANGED, so an AE drift between plate and shot stops reading as
    foreground (exercise_clean_plate_matting, 18_inpainting)
  * video exposure flicker - match frame N to frame 0 before background
    subtraction or flow (28_background_subtract_bgsegm, 29)
  * colour transfer - this formula in Lab IS Reinhard et al.: grade one
    shot to another, or a generated element to its plate (10, 11, 56)
  * stereo pairs - BM/SGBM assume brightness constancy (66, 80, 85)

PANORAMAS: you do NOT need this. 'CV Stitch (Advanced)' runs
cv2.detail's compensator itself (exposure_compensation = gain_blocks by
default) and plain 'CV Stitch' does it internally. Reach for the
blueprint when you own the warp yourself (exercise_stitch_two_views,
exercise_seam_pipeline), where the mask is the warped overlap. Measured
on boat1/boat2 - which really were metered differently - the residual
in the overlap goes 17.1 raw -> 7.7 detail.GainCompensator -> 7.1
BlocksGain -> 6.1 with this blueprint: every cv2.detail compensator is
GAIN-ONLY (its whole API is getMatGains/setMatGains), and that pair's
difference is nearly pure OFFSET.

WHEN NOT TO USE IT: HDR brackets (the exposure difference IS the
signal), NCC template matching and ECC alignment (already invariant to
gain+offset), and any mask whose content genuinely differs between the
two images - that bias is real, and it lands in the fit.

nodes.title: TILE 1 mask - where tile 1 is measured
[CV White Balance (xphoto)] WHOLE-IMAGE pass = the reference
[CV White Balance (xphoto)] Tile 1, balanced on its own
[CV White Balance (xphoto)] Tile 2, balanced on its own
TILED: each half found its own gains
[CV Exposure Match (Masked Per-Channel)] Match TILE 1 to the reference, measured inside tile 1
[CV Exposure Match (Masked Per-Channel)] Match TILE 2 to the reference, measured inside tile 2
MATCHED: the tile seam is gone
[CV Contrast (CLAHE/Equalize)] Tile 1, CLAHE on its own
[CV Contrast (CLAHE/Equalize)] Tile 2, CLAHE on its own
TILED: each half got its own tone curve
[CV Exposure Match (Masked Per-Channel)] Match TILE 1 to the reference (same node as above)
[CV Exposure Match (Masked Per-Channel)] Match TILE 2 to the reference (same node as above)
STILL WRONG: a tone curve is not a gain and an offset

groups.title: THE TWO TILES, AND A MASK FOR EACH - where every fit is measured
1. WHITE BALANCE PER TILE - a gain+offset drift, and it IS fixed
2. CLAHE PER TILE - a tone-curve drift, and it is NOT fixed (same wiring, same masks)
